robotic-surgery.a: Robotic-assisted joint replacement is a knee or hip surgery in which a computer-guided robotic platform helps the surgeon plan and execute bone cuts with sub-millimetre precision. The surgeon remains fully in control — the robot improves accuracy, alignment, and ligament balance, leading to better long-term implant survival and more natural movement.

robotic-surgery.q: Which robotic system does DHS Hospital use?
robotic-surgery.a: DHS Multispecialty Hospital uses the VELYS Robotic-Assisted Solution from Johnson & Johnson DePuy Synthes. VELYS is an imageless platform — no pre-operative CT scan is needed — and is the fastest-growing robotic knee platform in India since its November 2022 launch. It is paired with the J&J Attune knee implant system.

robotic-surgery.q: How is VELYS different from Mako or ROSA robotic systems?
robotic-surgery.a: Mako (Stryker) and ROSA (Zimmer) are CT-based: they require a pre-operative CT scan and extra radiation. VELYS is imageless and uses intra-operative anatomy mapping instead, which means no pre-op CT cost, no extra radiation, and a faster surgical workup. All major robotic platforms deliver excellent accuracy in experienced hands; the choice often comes down to surgeon preference and implant compatibility.

robotic-surgery.q: Is robotic knee replacement covered by insurance?
robotic-surgery.a: Yes. VELYS robotic knee replacement is covered by most Indian health insurance policies and TPAs. DHS Multispecialty Hospital is empaneled with major insurers and offers cashless processing. For a personalised written estimate, call our billing desk at +91 9081021444 before admission.

robotic-surgery.q: How long is recovery after robotic knee replacement at DHS?
robotic-surgery.a: Most patients stand and walk aided on day 0, are discharged in 2–3 days, walk without aids in 1–2 weeks, return to normal daily activities (including driving) in 4–6 weeks, and reach full recovery with complete range of motion at 3–4 months. Early mobilisation and structured physiotherapy at DHS shorten the recovery curve.

robotic-surgery.q: Who is a candidate for robotic joint replacement?
robotic-surgery.a: Candidates are typically patients with advanced osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or post-traumatic joint damage in the knee or hip whose pain and stiffness are not relieved by medication, physiotherapy, or injections. Robotic surgery is suitable for both primary replacement and revision cases.

robotic-surgery.q: Is robotic surgery safer than conventional joint replacement?
robotic-surgery.a: Robotic-assisted surgery delivers complication rates comparable to manual surgery performed by experienced surgeons, while reducing alignment error. Published data on VELYS shows strong alignment accuracy compared with manual technique, which is associated with better implant longevity and lower revision risk over 15–20 years.

robotic-surgery.q: Who performs robotic joint replacement at DHS Hospital?
robotic-surgery.a: The DHS robotic joint replacement programme is led by Dr. Hardik Shah (Medical Director, MS Orthopedic, FRCS Germany) and Dr. Swagat Shah (FIAAS UK). The DHS knee programme has successfully performed 2,000+ knee replacement surgeries (robotic and conventional) with high patient satisfaction.

robotic-surgery.q: How do I book a robotic knee replacement consultation at DHS?
robotic-surgery.a: Book online via the DHS Multispecialty Hospital website appointment page, call +91 9081610444, or visit the hospital reception in Gurukul, Ahmedabad. No referral is required; bring previous X-rays/MRIs and current medications.

joint-replacement.a: Joint replacement is recommended when severe arthritis, joint damage from injury, or chronic pain limits daily activities and conservative treatments (medication, physiotherapy, injections) no longer provide relief. Common candidates have advanced osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, or post-traumatic joint damage in the knee, hip, or shoulder.

joint-replacement.q: How long is recovery after knee replacement surgery?
joint-replacement.a: Most patients walk with support within 24–48 hours of surgery, are discharged in 3–5 days, and resume normal daily activities in 6–8 weeks. Full recovery and return to low-impact sport typically takes 3–6 months. Early mobilisation and structured physiotherapy at DHS shorten the recovery curve.

joint-replacement.q: What is the cost of knee replacement surgery in Ahmedabad?
joint-replacement.a: Cost varies by implant type (standard, high-flex, robotic-assisted), unilateral vs bilateral, and room category. DHS Multispecialty Hospital is empaneled with major insurers and TPAs and offers cashless treatment. Contact billing at +91 9081021444 for a written estimate before admission.

joint-replacement.q: Is robotic-assisted joint replacement available at DHS?
joint-replacement.a: Yes. DHS offers VELYS robotic-assisted knee replacement (Johnson & Johnson DePuy Synthes) — an imageless platform with no pre-operative CT scan, sub-millimetre accuracy, and the J&J Attune knee implant. Performed by Dr. Hardik Shah and Dr. Swagat Shah, who lead the robotic and conventional knee replacement programme at DHS. See the dedicated VELYS Robotic Knee Replacement page for full details, cost, and recovery timeline.

joint-replacement.q: How long does a knee or hip implant last?
joint-replacement.a: Modern knee and hip implants are designed to last 20–25 years in over 90% of patients. Longevity depends on implant material, patient weight, activity level, and surgical accuracy.

trauma.q: What is considered an orthopedic trauma emergency?
trauma.a: Fractures, dislocations, polytrauma from road accidents, open wounds with bone exposure, and crush injuries are orthopedic trauma emergencies that need immediate evaluation. DHS runs a 24/7 trauma service — call +91 9081610444.

trauma.q: Does DHS Hospital handle polytrauma cases?
trauma.a: Yes. DHS provides round-the-clock polytrauma care with on-call orthopedic, neurosurgery, vascular, and critical-care specialists, supported by a 24/7 ICU and operation theatres.

trauma.q: How quickly should a fracture be treated?
trauma.a: Closed fractures should be assessed within hours; open fractures require surgical washout within 6 hours to reduce infection risk. Call DHS Emergency at +91 9081610444 for immediate triage.

arthroscopy.a: Arthroscopy is a minimally invasive surgical technique that uses a small camera (arthroscope) inserted through a 5–10 mm incision to diagnose and treat joint problems. It results in less pain, smaller scars, and faster recovery than open surgery.

arthroscopy.q: What conditions can arthroscopic surgery treat?
arthroscopy.a: Arthroscopy treats meniscus tears, ACL/PCL injuries, rotator cuff tears, cartilage damage, loose bodies, and shoulder instability in the knee, shoulder, elbow, ankle, and hip joints.

arthroscopy.q: How long does arthroscopy recovery take?
arthroscopy.a: Diagnostic arthroscopy: 1–2 weeks. ACL reconstruction or rotator cuff repair: 4–6 months for full sport return. Most patients are discharged the same day or the next day.

spine-surgery.a: Spine surgery is recommended when conservative treatment (medication, physiotherapy, injections) fails to relieve symptoms of disc herniation, spinal stenosis, scoliosis, spinal injury, or progressive neurological deficit.

spine-surgery.q: Is minimally invasive spine surgery available?
spine-surgery.a: Yes. DHS offers minimally invasive spine procedures including microdiscectomy and minimally invasive fusion, which reduce blood loss, scar size, and hospital stay.

sports-medicine.a: Sports medicine is a specialty focused on injuries and conditions related to physical activity. It covers ACL tears, meniscus injuries, tendinopathies, stress fractures, and rehabilitation back to peak performance.
Yes. Anyone with an active lifestyle — recreational players, dancers, gym-goers, or labourers with overuse injuries — can benefit from our sports medicine programme.

cardiology.q: When should I see a cardiologist?
cardiology.a: See a cardiologist if you experience chest pain, breathlessness on exertion, palpitations, dizziness, fainting, swollen ankles, or have a family history of heart disease, diabetes, or high cholesterol.
Yes. DHS runs a 24/7 cardiac emergency service with ECG, 2D Echo, and ICU support. Call +91 9081610444 for chest pain or suspected heart attack.

cardiology.q: What heart tests are available at DHS?
cardiology.a: DHS offers ECG, 2D Echocardiography, Stress Testing (TMT), Holter monitoring, and preventive cardiology evaluations under one roof.

neurosurgery.a: Neurosurgery treats brain stroke, head injury, brain and spine tumours, epilepsy, hydrocephalus, slipped disc, and degenerative spine conditions. DHS combines neurology and neurosurgery for end-to-end care.
Yes. DHS offers 24/7 stroke evaluation with CT imaging and acute management. The first 4.5 hours after stroke onset ("golden window") are critical — call +91 9081610444 immediately.

cancer-surgery.q: What cancer treatments are offered at DHS?
cancer-surgery.a: DHS provides surgical oncology, cancer screening, chemotherapy day-care, palliative care, and cancer diagnostics including biopsy and imaging.

cancer-surgery.q: Do I need a referral for a cancer consultation?
cancer-surgery.a: No referral is required. Walk-in or book a consultation directly with our oncology team via the website or by calling +91 9081610444.

general-surgery.a: Laparoscopic (keyhole) surgery uses small incisions and a camera to perform abdominal procedures with less pain, smaller scars, and faster recovery than open surgery.

general-surgery.q: Which surgeries are commonly done laparoscopically at DHS?
general-surgery.a: Gallbladder removal, hernia repair, appendectomy, weight-loss (bariatric) surgery, and many gastrointestinal procedures are routinely performed laparoscopically at DHS.

icu.q: What facilities are available in the DHS ICU?
icu.a: Our 8-bed ICU has ventilator support, central monitoring, HEPA-filtered air, isolation rooms, and 24/7 critical-care intensivist and nursing coverage.
ICU visiting is restricted to 5 PM–6 PM daily to protect critically ill patients. One attendant briefing is provided once per day; emergency updates are available any time.

dialysis-unit.q: Is the DHS dialysis unit equipped for chronic kidney disease patients?
dialysis-unit.a: Yes. DHS has an exclusive 8-bed dialysis area with German-made dialysis machines, supporting both maintenance hemodialysis and acute kidney injury management.

dialysis-unit.q: Do you accept insurance and cashless dialysis?
dialysis-unit.a: Yes. DHS is empaneled with major insurance providers and TPAs for cashless dialysis. Contact billing at +91 9081021444.

radiology.a: DHS Radiology offers Digital X-Ray, 16-multislice CT scan, 3D/4D Sonography, Colour Doppler, and 2D Echocardiography under one roof, with same-day reporting for most studies.

radiology.q: Do I need an appointment for an X-Ray or sonography?
radiology.a: X-Rays are walk-in. Sonography, CT, and specialised studies need an appointment. Book online or call +91 9081610444.

orthopedics.q: What is robotic-assisted knee replacement, and how is it different from traditional knee replacement?
orthopedics.a: Robotic-assisted knee replacement uses the imageless VELYS robotic platform to create a real-time digital map of your knee during surgery, helping the surgeon make precise bone cuts and balance ligaments. Traditional knee replacement relies on manual instruments and pre-operative planning without live feedback.

orthopedics.q: Who is a good candidate for robotic knee replacement?
orthopedics.a: Adults with severe knee osteoarthritis, persistent knee pain, swelling, stiffness, or difficulty walking despite medicines and physiotherapy may be candidates. Older patients who are otherwise healthy can also benefit. The final decision is made after a clinical examination and review of X-rays.

orthopedics.q: How long does recovery take after robotic knee replacement at DHS Hospital?
orthopedics.a: Many patients are able to stand and walk with support on the same day as surgery. Light daily activities usually resume within 2–4 weeks, while full recovery and return to normal walking generally take 6–12 weeks. Our physiotherapy team guides each patient through a personalised rehab plan.

orthopedics.q: Who performs robotic knee replacement at DHS Hospital?
orthopedics.a: The procedure is led by Dr. Hardik M. Shah, Medical Director at DHS Multispecialty Hospital. He holds an MBBS, MS in Orthopedics, and FRCS (Germany), with over a decade of experience and more than 2,000 knee replacements performed. Dr. Swagat M. Shah also performs VELYS robotic knee replacement surgeries at DHS.

orthopedics.q: Is robotic knee replacement safe for elderly patients?
orthopedics.a: Yes. The imageless VELYS system avoids pre-operative CT radiation and allows smaller, more precise surgical steps, which can reduce soft-tissue trauma and support faster recovery. Every elderly patient is assessed individually for fitness before surgery.

orthopedics.q: What are the benefits of robotic knee replacement over traditional knee replacement?
orthopedics.a: Benefits include more accurate implant positioning, better ligament balance, less bone and tissue trauma, potentially less post-operative pain, and a faster return to walking. The robotic arm assists the surgeon; it does not operate independently.

orthopedics.q: Do I need a pre-operative CT scan for VELYS robotic knee replacement?
orthopedics.a: No. The VELYS system used at DHS is imageless — it builds a live digital model of your knee during the surgery itself, so a pre-operative CT scan is not required.

orthopedics.q: How do I book a consultation for knee pain at DHS Hospital?
orthopedics.a: You can book an appointment online through our appointment page or call us directly. Our orthopedics team will evaluate your symptoms, review your reports, and discuss whether robotic or traditional knee replacement is right for you.
